title_prefix: An inv never enters the announcing peer'
mechanism: Core inserts the announced hash into the announcing peer's m_tx_inventory_known_filter the moment a gen-tx inv arrives -- AddKnownTx(peer, inv.hash) at refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:4174, placed BEFORE the IsInitialBlockDownload gate at :4176 so it runs even during IBD; AddKnownTx itself is refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:1143-1150. That filter is the read side of both queue paths: PushTxInventory skips a peer whose filter already contains the hash (:2261-2263), and SendMessages re-checks it just before pushing an inv (:6067-6069) and inserts on send (:6083). Core keys it by the peer's PREFERRED id -- 'peer.m_wtxid_relay ? wtxid : txid' at :4491-4492 and the same expression when constructing the inv at :6064-6066 -- so the id inserted on inv receipt is exactly the id the relay path later looks up. Core also AddKnownTx's every unique parent of a rejected orphan (:3143). Ours: handle-inv (src/networking/protocol.lisp:754-853) records the announcement in the tx-request tracker and never touches peer-announced-txs. The filter is written only at src/networking/protocol.lisp:1851 (tx receipt), :3048 (inv flush) and :3105 (BIP35 mempool dump), and read at :2899 (relay-transaction) and :3041 (flush) -- every one of those five sites keys it by TXID, while a wtxidrelay peer's inv carries a wtxid. The orphan-parent arm of :3143 has no counterpart at all: the :missing-input branch (:1895-1905) writes nothing to the filter.
consequence: Bandwidth only, and bounded: one extra 36-byte inv entry per (transaction, peer that had already announced it to us and from which we did not download it). We do insert the delivering peer's txid at :1851, so the tx is not echoed to its sender; what is echoed goes to every OTHER peer that announced it during our trickle delay, which on a well-connected node is most of the tx-relay peer set. The peer discards the duplicate, so nothing is lost and no peer gains a lever -- it is wasted egress plus a needless confirmation to each announcer that its announcement reached us, which is the privacy reason Core keeps the filter. The parent arm adds the same waste for orphan parents we have just failed to use. S3: bounded inefficiency, no censorship or DoS lever, no transaction lost.
evidence: Probe ga11-txrelay-known-filter (scripts/dev.sh load + eval), warm image bitcoin-lisp-sbcl:2.6.5-4, *cached-is-ibd* bound NIL. (1) Case 1, one MSG_TX inv of a txid from a non-wtxidrelay peer through handle-inv, then relay-transaction of the same txid to that peer: (:TRACKED-ANNOUNCEMENT 1 :KNOWN-FILTER-HIT-TXID NIL :QUEUED-BACK 1) -- the announcement IS tracked, the filter is NOT written, and the tx is queued straight back. (2) Positive control, the same relay-transaction with the txid MANUALLY placed in peer-announced-txs: (:KNOWN-FILTER-HIT-TXID T :QUEUED-BACK 0) -- so the NIL above is a missing insert, not a dead check. (3) Case 2, a wtxidrelay peer announcing MSG_WTX, then Core's exact AddKnownTx(peer, inv.hash) simulated by inserting the WTXID, then relay-transaction with :wtxid: (:TRACKED-ANNOUNCEMENT 1 :KNOWN-FILTER-HIT-WTXID-AFTER-INV NIL :QUEUED-BACK-EVEN-WITH-WTXID-INSERTED 1) -- inserting the inv hash alone does not fix it, because the read side is txid-keyed. (4) Case 3, a parent of a rejected orphan: (:PARENT-QUEUED-BACK 1). Inv entry size measured at 36 bytes (a one-item getdata payload was 37 bytes = varint 1 + 36 in probe pC). Ours: src/networking/protocol.lisp:754-853, :1851, :2899, :3041, :3048, :3105, :1895-1905; src/networking/peer.lisp:125 (the filter is a 50,000-entry rejects filter, matching Core's CRollingBloomFilter{50000, 0.000001} at net_processing.cpp:307). Core at d3056bc: refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:1143-1150, :2250-2264, :3143, :4174-4178, :4491-4492, :6060-6084.
fix_shape: Give the known-tx filter Core's two missing writes and make it id-consistent. In handle-inv's gen-tx arm, insert the announced hash into peer-announced-txs for that peer before the IBD gate and before AddTxAnnouncement, exactly where Core puts AddKnownTx (net_processing.cpp:4174) -- note that Core places it OUTSIDE the !IsInitialBlockDownload branch on purpose, so a peer that announced during IBD is still not told about the transaction afterwards. Add the second write in the :missing-input branch of handle-tx: for each unique parent txid handed to request-orphan-parents, insert the parent into the delivering peer's filter (net_processing.cpp:3143). Both writes are useless on their own unless the filter is keyed the way Core keys it: switch peer-announced-txs to the peer's PREFERRED id -- wtxid for a wtxid-relay peer, txid otherwise -- at all five sites (protocol.lisp:1851, :2899, :3041, :3048, :3105), constructing the inv first and using its hash for the check, as Core's comment at net_processing.cpp:6061-6066 spells out. The parent arm stays txid-keyed on both sides because orphan parents are known only by txid. This does not widen the getdata anti-probing gate: that gate is peer-last-inv-sequence (protocol.lisp:2144-2160, Core's info_for_relay at net_processing.cpp:2496-2506), not this filter.
